intro: Long ago, builders made giant stone churches by hand. They used tools like the square, the level and the plumb line. Young helpers learned from skilled builders. The builders met in a hut called a lodge.

Later, many clubs took the name lodge. Members paid a little money so they could help each other. They helped sick workers, widows and children. Some lodges built hospitals. Chicago had a very tall lodge building.
In this unit, you will name a builder's tools. You will tell how clubs helped families. You will also learn what a kind club does when you ask it questions.
bigQuestion: How did builders and helpers make their towns stronger?

timeline.t: Builders start Notre-Dame, a big stone church in Paris.
Builders start Cologne Cathedral in Germany. It takes more than 600 years.
Someone writes a rule book in verse for builders in England.
A paper in Scotland lists questions to test the Mason Word.
The Odd Fellows start a lodge in Baltimore to help members.
A Prince Hall lodge meets in Chicago.
Chicago's tall Masonic Temple is finished.
Mooseheart, a town for children, opens in Illinois.
The first Shriners hospital for children opens in Louisiana.
A Shriners hospital for children opens in Chicago.

words.d: a worker who cuts stone and builds with it
a tool shaped like an L that checks a corner
a string with a weight that hangs straight down
a person who learns a job by working with a skilled worker
a builders' hut; later, a club or the room where its members meet
a person who belongs to a club or group
a place where doctors and nurses care for people who are sick or hurt

test.q: Who built big stone churches long ago?
test.why: Stonemasons cut stone and built churches, castles and walls.

test.q: Which tool shows if the top of a stone is flat?
test.why: A level shows if something is flat.

test.q: What did a builder tap with a wooden mallet?
test.why: A builder tapped a sharp chisel with a mallet to shape stone.

choices: A person learning a job from a skilled worker
test.why: An apprentice learns a job by working next to a skilled person, like Tom with Master John.

test.q: What was a lodge at a building site?
choices: A hut where builders met and worked
test.why: The first lodges were huts where builders kept tools, ate and worked.

test.q: Why did builders have the Mason Word?
choices: To show a builder was trained
test.why: The Mason Word was a password that showed a builder had learned the trade.

test.q: How did lodges help when a member was sick?
choices: They sent a doctor and money
test.why: Many lodges had a lodge doctor and gave sick members money each week.

test.q: What did the Shriners build for children?
test.why: The Shriners built children's hospitals, like the one in Chicago in 1926.

test.q: What was special about Chicago's Masonic Temple in 1892?
choices: It was one of the tallest buildings in the world
test.why: The 1892 Masonic Temple had more than 20 floors. It was one of the world's tallest.

test.q: A club asks you to hide something that hurts. What do you do?
test.why: No one should ask you to hide something that hurts. Always tell a trusted grown-up.

write.prompt: Were lodges good helpers for their towns? Tell or write your answer. Use two things you learned, like the lodge doctor, Mooseheart or the Shriners hospital.
tips: Tell one way a lodge helped a family.
Tell a second way, with a place or a year.
Use a unit word, like member or hospital.
